subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire
body:
From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

Team —

Forwarding NorthBridge’s retention/audit logging questionnaire (below). They’re asking for explicit retention ranges, “proof” of deletion, and legal hold semantics.

Can we turn around a consolidated response today? Target is EOD PT so Markus can attach to the security review packet.

Specific asks I need help validating:
- Default retention values (audit logs, admin activity, request metadata, telemetry)
- What is configurable in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private today vs “v1” timeline
- Legal hold behavior (what gets frozen, how applied, who can set)
- Exports (audit log export range and any warnings when older-than-retention)
- Evidence we can provide (screenshots of Console, runbook excerpt, control mapping)

Naomi: can you confirm product language + what we can commit for v1?
Olga: can you sanity check controls framing and what we can share externally?
Marcus/Kevin: need technical confirmation on enforcement + audit log export constraints.
Sofia/Michael: please flag anything that should be “under NDA / subject to contract” or can’t be asserted.

Thanks,
Aisha

—

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 9:20 AM PST
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Subject: Fwd: NorthBridge questionnaire

Fwd’ing the questionnaire text that Avery sent last night. They’re pushing for 365-day audit logs + 30-day telemetry unless legal hold.

From: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgefin.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 7:46 PM PST
Subject: Redwood Inference — Retention & Audit Logging Questions
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@northbridgefin.com>

Hi Markus,

As part of our security review, please answer the questions below (brief is fine):

1) What data categories do you retain related to customer usage (audit logs, admin activity, API request metadata, telemetry/analytics, operational logs)?
2) For each category, what is the default retention period? Are periods configurable per tenant? If yes, what min/max values are supported?
3) Do you support “legal hold” to prevent deletion? If yes, how is it applied and audited?
4) What is your deletion mechanism (TTL, scheduled deletion, compaction)? Is deletion verified/auditable?
5) Can we export audit logs for SIEM ingestion? What format, delivery method, and export window limitations apply?
6) Do you retain inference payload content (prompts, completions) by default? If optional, what controls exist?
7) Please provide any SOC 2 / ISO-aligned documentation or control mappings relevant to retention and audit logging.

Thank you,
Avery Chen
Security Engineering
NorthBridge Financial



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

Aisha —

Product language proposal (please adjust as needed):

- We support tenant-configurable retention controls for specific datasets in v1 (audit logs + admin activity + selected telemetry tables). Some infra/operational logs remain governed by SRE/vendor constraints and are not currently customer-configurable.
- Hosted/Dedicated: retention configurable per tenant; Private: depends on deployment mode, but we can align to customer retention requirements and provide enforcement documentation.
- Guardrails: we enforce minimum retention for auditability/security investigations; we also support maximum retention and do not allow “never delete” except in explicit legal hold scenarios.

On “prompts/completions”: we should say we do not retain raw inference payload content by default beyond transient processing, except where customers explicitly enable logging features (and even then, it’s request metadata vs content, depending on configuration). If we’re not ready to commit, keep it high-level.

I’ll defer to Marcus/Kevin on exact defaults and min/max.

Naomi


From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

Technical notes on audit logs + exports:

1) Audit log coverage (what’s in scope):
- Console/admin actions (e.g., key creation/rotation, retention policy changes, RBAC changes, org/tenant admin events)
- Authn/authz events for admin surfaces
- Selected control-plane operations

2) Default retention (current):
- Hosted/Dedicated audit logs: 365 days default
- Admin activity logs: aligned to audit logs (365 days)

3) Configurable retention (v1):
- Supported: 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days (tenant-configurable), with minimum 30 for audit logs.
- Legal hold: can override deletion (see Marcus note, but enforcement worker checks hold flag before delete).

4) Export:
- Export format: JSON Lines (one event per line) + optional CSV (limited fields) via Console download and API endpoint.
- Export window: exports are limited to retained data (i.e., you can’t export what’s already beyond retention). We include metadata in export response indicating the tenant’s effective retention and the earliest available timestamp.
- SIEM: we have a supported pull model today (API + signed URL). Push connectors are in roadmap; we can provide guidance for Splunk/Datadog ingestion.

Caveat: in Private, export depends on customer network constraints; we can still provide formats and API, but delivery is within customer environment.

Kevin


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 11:23 AM PST
Subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

Adding enforcement + “proof” language.

Deletion mechanism:
- Hybrid approach: where datastore supports native TTL/partition expiration we use it; otherwise we run scheduled deletion jobs (batched, rate-limited, idempotent).
- For audit logs specifically, it’s scheduled deletion with safety rails:
  - fixed batch sizes + max DB load thresholds
  - deletes are scoped by tenant + dataset + cutoff timestamp
  - job emits metrics (rows deleted, lag, error counts) and writes an audit event summarizing each run

Auditability/verification:
- Console shows: effective retention policy, last enforcement run time, and exceptions/holds (v1 screen)
- We can provide evidence via:
  - screenshots of the retention settings + enforcement status
  - a redacted excerpt of the runbook (how we validate deletions)
  - change audit events when retention settings are modified

Legal hold:
- “Legal hold” is implemented as a tenant-scoped flag with optional dataset scoping (audit logs/admin activity eligible). When present, enforcement job skips deletes for covered datasets.
- Legal hold changes generate an audit log entry (who/when/what).

Telemetry:
- Selected analytics tables will have partition TTLs; default currently 90 days, configurable to 30/90/180 (we should confirm if we want to promise 180).

Marcus


From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Daniel Carter <daniel.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 12:05 PM PST
Subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

From a GRC standpoint:

- We can share a “baseline compliance reporting pack” under NDA. Keep it labeled DRAFT and “for security review purposes only.”
- For Q7 (SOC 2/ISO): don’t claim certification status in this response. Instead: “SOC 2/ISO-aligned controls and evidence” + offer to share our latest report under NDA where applicable.
- Control framing (high level):
  - Data retention policy exists, is documented, and enforced by technical controls
  - Audit logging covers privileged actions and is protected from modification
  - Retention changes are restricted to authorized admins and are auditable

Daniel and I can attach:
- Draft pack PDF
- A 1-page control-to-evidence matrix excerpt focused on retention/audit logging (or we can embed bullets in the response)

Olga


From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 12:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: NorthBridge security review — retention controls + audit logging questionnaire

Legal/commercial notes:

- For “legal hold,” avoid implying Redwood will determine legal requirements for them. Phrase as: “We support a legal hold mechanism to suspend deletion upon customer request / contractual or legal requirement.”
- Avoid absolute statements like “we do not retain prompts/completions.” Safer: “By default, we do not persist inference payload content as part of standard logging; customers can choose configurations that may increase logged data. We can provide details for your configuration.”
- For Private, avoid hard product commitments unless in SOW. Say: “We can align retention to customer requirements in Private deployments, subject to deployment architecture and contract.”

Sofia


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgefin.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@northbridgefin.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 4:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Inference — Retention & Audit Logging Questions
Attachments: Redwood_Compliance_Reporting_Pack_v1_DRAFT.pdf, NorthBridge_Retention_AuditLogging_Questionnaire_Response_v0.4.docx

Hi Avery, hi Priya —

Thank you for the clear questions. Please find attached our questionnaire response and a draft of our baseline compliance reporting pack (shared for security review purposes).

A few highlights:
- We maintain audit logs covering privileged/admin actions and key control-plane operations. Default audit log retention is 365 days, and we support tenant-configurable retention options with guardrails.
- We support audit log export (JSON Lines; optional CSV for limited fields) and exports are constrained to the retention window (the response includes how we surface the earliest available timestamp).
- We support a legal hold mechanism to suspend deletion upon request/requirement, and changes to retention/hold settings are themselves auditable.

If helpful, we can schedule 30 minutes early next week to walk through the retention controls UI and how enforcement/auditability works.

Best,
Aisha Rahman, PhD
Exec Sponsor, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
